Russia strikes Kyiv bridge as Germany’s Merz visits, pledges aid
Merz and Zelensky were due to meet as Germany and Ukraine neared a deal for a new package of military support worth more than US$1 billion
Russia struck a bridge in Kyiv on Sunday soon after Germany’s chancellor arrived in Ukraine’s capital on a surprise visit to demonstrate European support in the face of an upsurge in attacks.
Air raid sirens blared across Kyiv, urging residents to shelter soon after Friedrich Merz arrived under tight security, with warnings of approaching Russian attack drones.
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko then confirmed that a strike had damaged the road surface on the Northern Bridge – one of several connecting the eastern and western parts of the city over the Dnipro River which have been struck in recent days.
Images posted on messaging channels appeared to show a missile slamming into the structure, sending a fireball into the air.

articles.title: Iran refutes ‘Big Lies’ on nuclear program, drug production
articles.body:
Iran refutes ‘Big Lies’ on nuclear program, drug production
TEHRAN— Iran’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations and other international organizations in Vienna has rejected US allegations that Iran was producing drugs at its nuclear facilities, describing the claim as another “BIG LIE” aimed at creating pretexts for aggression against the country.
In a message posted on X on Sunday, the mission said Iran’s record in combating the global drug problem could be independently verified by the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the International Narcotics Control Board (INCB).
“After the BIG LIE of Iranian nuclear weapons, another BIG LIE on ‘doing drugs’ soared,” the mission said, adding, “But a liar ought to have a good memory.”
The Iranian mission also pointed to the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) continuous monitoring of Iran’s nuclear facilities, saying the agency had maintained around-the-clock surveillance of the facilities under safeguards.
“Irrespective of Iran’s outstanding contribution to addressing [the] world drug problem — which could be simply confirmed by UNODC and INCB — Iran nuclear facilities were constantly monitored by the IAEA 24/7,” it said.
The mission called on the IAEA to expose 'false allegations concerning Iranian nuclear facilities subject to safeguards.'
It further argued that allegations regarding nuclear weapons and illicit drug production were being used to manufacture justifications for military action against Iran.
“Looks that inventing pretexts is easier than admitting that invading, bombing and plundering other nations is about domination — not democracy, non-proliferation or as recently claimed, illicit drugs,” the mission said. “The narrative might change, but the facts remain.”
Addressing US President Donald Trump directly, the Iranian mission urged Washington to stop the 'manufacture of pretexts and openly acknowledge its alleged interest in Iran’s strategic resources.'
“Stop manufacturing pretexts. Say plainly that you dreamed about taking over Iran’s strategic resources, oil and gas, and independence,” it said.
The statement followed remarks by Trump at a rally in Durant, Oklahoma, in which he claimed that Iran had been “doing drugs” at “drug factories” and “nuclear factories.”
Trump also claimed that the alleged facilities had been “hit so hard,” linking the assertions to his justification for the US military aggression against Iran seven months earlier.

articles.title: Poland, Romania Reject Ukraine Appeal for Grain Transit Help
articles.body:
Poland and Romania have rejected appeals by Ukraine to expand agricultural transit corridors and provide financial subsidies to export millions of metric tons of trapped grain through Europe, Politico reported.
The refusal follows a diplomatic mission to Brussels earlier in the week by Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Taras Vysotskyi, who met directly with EU counterparts to request transit authorization for larger cargo volumes alongside €1.1 billion ($1.2 billion) in financial assistance to offset elevated freight costs.

Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“It’s very, very critical,” Vysotskyi told Politico, warning that Russian kinetic strikes against Ukrainian Black Sea ports and commercial vessels, now entering their third consecutive month, have paralyzed conventional maritime export routes.
Vysotskyi stated that harvested grain and oilseed stockpiles are accumulating rapidly inside domestic storage silos, depriving Ukrainian agricultural enterprises of the working capital necessary to purchase seeds, fuel, and fertilizers for the upcoming planting season.
“If the situation remains like this until spring, it could mean a reduction in sown areas next year of even 35 to 40 percent,” Vysotskyi cautioned, pointing to the risk of compounded harvest contractions in 2027.
Domestic farm protections
Neighboring Central and Eastern European governments maintain that their regional transport networks and maritime terminals cannot absorb additional Ukrainian freight without displacing domestic producers.
Kulbergs’ Pro-Ukraine Party Wins Latvian Election
Romanian Agriculture Minister Barna Tánczos confirmed that Bucharest will not accommodate higher Ukrainian export volumes, emphasizing that protecting local agricultural markets remains the Romanian government’s core priority.
Tánczos explained that existing transit volumes, combined with seasonal low water levels along the Danube River, have already overwhelmed Romanian ports such as Constanța, leaving domestic farmers unable to offload and market their own harvests.
“The interest for our own farmers remains a priority,” Tánczos told Politico. “Everyone knows that we cannot double the number of trains, we cannot double the capacity of roads, railways, and ports.”
Poland’s Ministry of Infrastructure delivered an identical rebuff, informing reporters that the Polish government is “not planning any changes aimed at increasing the transit of Ukrainian agricultural products.”
Black Sea maritime blockade
The transit impasse coincides with sustained Russian strikes targeting Ukrainian maritime hubs and commercial shipping across the northwestern Black Sea.
Over recent months, Russian missile and drone bombardments have repeatedly hit port elevators, container berths, and civilian cargo vessels docked across Odesa, Chornomorsk, and Pivdennyi, increasing maritime freight insurance premiums and constraining commercial navigation through Ukraine’s unilateral coastal corridor.
The mounting operational hazards were underscored in recent diplomatic representations. Since late June, at least 25 Turkish-owned or Turkish-operated merchant vessels have been damaged or caught in crossfire in the Black Sea, prompting Ankara to launch a multilateral mediation initiative.
A Turkish diplomat confirmed that Ankara transmitted a draft memorandum of understanding to both Kyiv and Moscow seeking a formal cessation of kinetic strikes directed at commercial maritime traffic and civilian port installations.
The diplomatic proposal is modeled partially on the Black Sea Grain Initiative, the wartime agreement brokered in July 2022 by Turkey and the UN that facilitated the export of nearly 33 million metric tons of Ukrainian foodstuffs through a protected maritime corridor before Russia unilaterally abandoned the arrangement in July 2023.

articles.title: Germany to fund tens of thousands of interceptor drones for Ukraine
articles.body:
Germany to fund tens of thousands of interceptor drones for Ukraine
Germany will fund the procurement of tens of thousands of interceptor drones for Ukraine's defence forces. The funding is part of Germany's winter military assistance package.
Source: Ukrainska Pravda, citing the press service for Quantum Systems
Details: The procurement of interceptor drones was announced by Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz during his visit to Kyiv on 4 October. Berlin will fund drones developed by the Quantum WIY Industries team, which is a joint project of Ukraine's WIY Drones and Germany's Quantum Systems.
Quote from press service: "The drones will be produced in Ukraine, so the manufacturing of interceptors will expand precisely as the need for protection against Russian strike drones grows. Thanks to this order, production of the interception systems already in use in Ukraine will scale up."
Details: Merz also met with representatives of the German company during his visit to Kyiv. Specifically, the manufacturers plan to expand UAV production in Ukraine in response to the intensifying Russian attacks involving jet-powered drones.
Quote from Sven Kruck, Co-CEO of Quantum Systems: "Ukraine needs interceptor drones at an industrial scale. By expanding production in Ukraine, we can respond more quickly to the immediate threat while simultaneously building industrial capacity that will also strengthen Germany and its allies."
Details: Furthermore, the company said that Quantum Systems signed a memorandum with Ukraine's Fire Point at a defence industry roundtable attended by Chancellor Merz and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
"The companies will jointly develop unmanned technologies and assets to counter modern aerial aircraft," the press service said.
Background:
- Ukrainska Pravda reported that in April 2026, Ukraine's WIY and Germany's Quantum Systems signed a memorandum of cooperation to establish a joint venture for the production of WIY Strila anti-Shahed interceptors.
- In August 2026, Ukrainian soldiers began testing the Spys interceptor drone from WIY Drones, developed to counter jet-powered UAVs. The initial batch of 50 drones was delivered to units for combat testing.

articles.title: Taliban Delegation Participates in Russia’s Center-2026 Exercises
articles.body:
A Taliban military delegation took part in Russia’s Center-2026 strategic military exercises at Moscow’s invitation.
The official page of the Ministry of Defense of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan reported the participation.
The Taliban representatives observed the drills and toured an exhibition showcasing Russian military equipment and weapons.
During the visit, the Afghan delegation also met with military representatives from other countries who had arrived for the exercises.
This is the first time that a Taliban military delegation has been invited to attend Russian military exercises as observers since the Taliban returned to power in 2021.
Center-2026 is a large-scale Russian strategic military exercise during which Russian forces practiced operations in the Central Asian direction and the Caspian region. Moscow invited military contingents and observers from dozens of countries to take part.
Military contingents from Belarus, China, Kyrgyzstan, Mongolia, Pakistan, and Tajikistan participated in the exercises. Kazakhstan and the Republic of the Congo sent operational groups, while representatives of 33 other countries, including Afghanistan, India, North Korea, and Vietnam, attended as observers.
The delegation’s participation reflected the growing political and military ties between Russia and Afghanistan.
A key development in bilateral relations was the signing of a military-technical cooperation agreement. On May 27, 2026, Russia and the Taliban signed the agreement.
Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu and Taliban Defense Minister Moulavi Mohammad Yaqoob Mujahid signed the agreement. The exact scope of the agreement remains unclear, as the document’s text has not been made public.
However, while explaining the agreement to the media, Russia’s special envoy for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, said it primarily covers refurbishing military equipment already in the Taliban’s possession. In the future, the two sides could conclude separate defense contracts.
The Russian side also said it was considering the possibility of establishing training centers for Taliban technical personnel responsible for maintaining military equipment.

articles.title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine
articles.body:
Smoke comes out from a pharma plant struck in Ukraine’s Sumy on Sunday
Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Ukraine’s Sumy Sunday in what Kusum Group cofounder Sanjeev Gupta described as a “targeted attack”, killing an engineer and injuring some others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed.Speaking to TOI, Gupta said the attack was not an isolated incident and claimed that pharmaceutical and food facilities in Ukraine had also come under attack over the past month. “Six drones hit the factory. So, it is a targeted attack. It’s not by chance. Actually, for the last one month, they are attacking all pharma and food items also,” Gupta said.The plant was operational when the strikes took place, Gupta said. The engineering department was hit and one engineer was killed, while other workers were evacuated.Gupta said the extent of damage could keep the plant out of operation for at least one to two years.“We are not able to evaluate the losses right now. We will come to know more tomorrow. But as per my understanding, we will not run this plant in the near future,” he added.
In a statement issued later Sunday, Kusum Healthcare Pvt Ltd said total damage from the attack was projected to breach the $50 million mark.
The company said its India business and management were reviewing the situation as the extent of the destruction emerged. The Sumy facility covers around 50,000 sq metres and has five blocks, Gupta said.It has been manufacturing medicines in Ukraine since 2009, including products for segments such as cardiology and gastroenterology. Gupta said Kusum is the biggest Indian pharmaceutical company operating in Ukraine, with a market share of more than 3%. The latest attack is not the first major strike on Kusum’s Ukrainian operations.The company said its warehouse was destroyed by a Russian drone on April 14, 2025, with losses from that attack exceeding UAH 1 billion.Despite the latest setback, Gupta said the group plans to continue its business in Ukraine.
